task.instructions:
Using matplotlib, draw a GROUPED (side-by-side) bar chart of a survey's response breakdown across four topics. Values are percent of respondents choosing each response; each topic's three values sum to 100:
  Remote Work:      Agree 62, Neutral 21, Disagree 17
  Four-Day Week:    Agree 71, Neutral 18, Disagree 11
  AI Coding Tools:  Agree 45, Neutral 30, Disagree 25
  Open Floor Plans: Agree 28, Neutral 24, Disagree 48
Requirements:
1. One group of three bars per topic, with the topics running Remote Work, Four-Day Week, AI Coding Tools, Open Floor Plans from left to right.
2. Inside each topic's group the bars must appear in the order Agree, Neutral, Disagree from left to right.
3. The bars must be side by side, NOT stacked: every bar starts at y = 0 and no two bars share the same x position.
4. The x tick labels must be the four topic names, in the order above.
5. Include a legend whose entries are exactly Agree, Neutral, Disagree.
6. The y axis must start at 0 and represent percent.
7. Add a dashed horizontal reference line at y = 50.
8. Add a text annotation naming whichever topic has the highest Disagree share and stating that share, in the form `Highest disagreement: <topic> (<value>%)`.
9. Give the chart a title and label both axes.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Data
labels = ['Remote Work', 'Four-Day Week', 'AI Coding Tools', 'Open Floor Plans']
agree = [62, 71, 28, 45]
neutral = [21, 18, 30, 24]
disagree = [17, 11, 25, 48]

# Find topic with highest disagree
max_disagree_idx = np.argmax(disagree)
max_disagree_topic = labels[max_disagree_idx]
max_disagree_value = disagree[max_disagree_idx]

# Plot
x = np.arange(len(labels))  # the label locations
width = 0.25  # the width of the bars

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

# Plot bars
rects1 = ax.bar(x - width, agree, width, label='Agree', color='#1f77b4')
rects2 = ax.bar(x, neutral, width, label='Neutral', color='#ff7f0e')
rects3 = ax.bar(x + width, disagree, width, label='Disagree', color='#2ca02c')

# Add horizontal reference line
ax.axhline(y=50, color='gray', linestyle='--')

# Add labels, title, and legend
ax.set_ylabel('Percent (%)')
ax.set_xlabel('Topics')
ax.set_title('Survey Agreement Breakdown')
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(labels)
ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
ax.legend()

# Add annotation for highest disagreement
ax.text(0.5, 0.95, f'Highest disagreement: {max_disagree_topic} ({max_disagree_value}%)', 
        transform=ax.transAxes, ha='center', bbox=dict(facecolor='white', alpha=0.8))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('figure.png')
EOF"}

cat << 'EOF' > plot_survey_agreement.py
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Data
labels = ['Remote Work', 'Four-Day Week', 'AI Coding Tools', 'Open Floor Plans']
agree = [62, 71, 45, 28]
neutral = [21, 18, 30, 24]
disagree = [17, 11, 25, 48]

# Find topic with highest disagree
max_disagree_idx = np.argmax(disagree)
max_disagree_topic = labels[max_disagree_idx]
max_disagree_value = disagree[max_disagree_idx]

# Plot
x = np.arange(len(labels))  # the label locations
width = 0.25  # the width of the bars

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

# Plot bars
rects1 = ax.bar(x - width, agree, width, label='Agree', color='#1f77b4')
rects2 = ax.bar(x, neutral, width, label='Neutral', color='#ff7f0e')
rects3 = ax.bar(x + width, disagree, width, label='Disagree', color='#2ca02c')

# Add horizontal reference line
ax.axhline(y=50, color='gray', linestyle='--')

# Add labels, title, and legend
ax.set_ylabel('Percent (%)')
ax.set_xlabel('Topics')
ax.set_title('Survey Agreement Breakdown')
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(labels)
ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
ax.legend()

# Add annotation for highest disagreement
ax.text(0.5, 0.95, f'Highest disagreement: {max_disagree_topic} ({max_disagree_value}%)', 
        transform=ax.transAxes, ha='center', bbox=dict(facecolor='white', alpha=0.8))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('figure.png')
EOF
